column1: # Contract cases of the play to core hooks for block changes (docs/protocol/29-block-updates-and-placement.md
# §7 "How clients learn about block changes", 09-cobolcraft-profile.md §3.2 rows 0x04, 0x08, 0x29, 0x42, 0x31).
# Read by tools/gen/gen_contract.py; see README.md. The player is Alice (creative, joined in memory), the
# world is the test world; the texts are the packets the player is sent, as CORETEST.cpy TEST-DRAIN-BLOCKS
# writes them: Light Update 49(chunk x,chunk z), Block Update 8(x,y,z=state), Block Changed Ack 4(sequence).
# Packet order, from doc 29 §7: a chunk holder's broadcast sends the Light Update first (§7.2 step 1) and the
# Block Update after it (step 2); the Block Changed Ack is sent last (§7.3: at the start of the connection's
# next tick, after the broadcasts of the tick); a rejected action re-sends the authoritative Block Update
# directly, and the ack still follows it (§7.3).
# State ids and the baseplate (state 1, never broken) are standin-content §1.1; greystone is state 2, void 0.
# A row id starting with `!` marks a documented behaviour the code does not have yet (README.md): such a row
# passes while the code differs and fails when it matches, so that mark is then removed.
# seam: play-core-blocks

# paths: contract/cases/play-core-blocks.tsv core/src/blocks.cob core/src/breaking.cob core/src/light.cob core/src/play.cob core/src/world.cob client/src/sp-host.cob docs/protocol/29-block-updates-and-placement.md
